newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit recovers from news report.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit recovers from news report.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit recovered its composure by noon on Thursday after shedding some 20-30 points in early trade on an erroneous media report.

Dealers said the ringgit hit a low of 2.5040 to the U.S. dollar on a media report quoting U.S. Trade Rep. Charlene Barshefsky as saying Malaysia would be graduated from the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) next week.
A U.S. embassy spokesman in Kuala Lumpur denied the report, adding there had been no changes to the previously stated schedule to graduate GSP from Malaysia on January 1, 1997.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5023/33 per dollar at 0430 GMT against 2.5015/18 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
"That (the report) was the highlight of the day. But people realised it almost immediately and corrected their positions," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.

A treasury manager with a Japanese bank in Singapore said the sell-off was a knee-jerk reaction and the ringgit was unlikely to suffer in the medium- to long-term even if the United States did withdraw Malaysia's special trade privileges.
He said dollar/ringgit looked well supported around 2.5000/10, with its upside capped at 2.5050.
Another Japanese bank dealer in Singapore said the dollar had a strong chance of breaking above 2.5050 in the next day or two as long as it held above 2.5000/10.
In Indonesia, the rupiah gained from concern about a liquidity crunch on Friday, which also spurred players to buy short-dated swaps.
A foreign bank dealer in Jakarta said operators were unclear about actual liquidity conditions on Friday but some players seemed to use it as an excuse to drive the swap market up.
"In fact last Friday supply wasn't that tight compared to the previous two Fridays. But the psychological impact is still felt," he said.

A local bank dealer said some players were also seen trying to squeeze offshore players who had gone long on dollars early this week following top officials' comments on the rupiah's depreciation target and intervention band.
Spot rupiah was at 2,323.25/23.75 at 0440 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,324.5/25.0.
The U.S. bank dealer said rises in short-dated swap rates seemed to have also caused longer-term premiums to follow.
He said offshore operators' confidence in the rupiah was reaffirmed after Wednesday's positive inflation and trade data.
The Thai baht slid in line with the dollar's continued strong tone after it rose above 112 yen overnight for the first time in 32 months.
The overnight interbank rate was at around 9.00-9.50 percent in early trade and swap premiums declined as foreign funds continued to flow into the country.
"The baht has a better outlook since (Pime Minister) Banharn announced his resignation," said the treasury manager at the Singapore-based Japanese bank.
The Singapore dollar remained on soft ground after falling below the psychologically important 1.4100 level against its U.S. counterpart overnight.
"The market took its cue from the overnight move this morning. But profit-taking interest in the ringgit/Sing cross will cap dollar/Sing," said the Japanese bank dealer.
He said ringgit/Sing would face resistance around 0.5640/45. It was quoted at 0.5635/38 at midday.
Dealers said talk of large U.S. dollar sell orders around S$1.4120 would also limit the Singapore unit's weakness.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
